data.name: Lavitraj
data.gender_notes: Lavitraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lavitraj is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Lavana' meaning 'clarifying' and 'Tri' meaning 'three'. In Hindu mythology, Lavitraj is known as the god Vishwakarma's messenger. He is believed to bring prosperity, wealth, and success. The name Lavitraj carries the meaning “God's Messenger” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lavitraj usually hope their child will grow to embody god's messenger and live with faith, good character and purpose.

vedic_reference.note: The name 'Lavitraj' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'लवन' (Lavan) meaning 'Light' and 'राजा' (Raja) meaning 'King'. It is a combination of the two words and represents a radiant and shining king.

historical_references.reference: Lavitraj was a legendary king of the Haihayas, a dynasty that ruled parts of the Indian subcontinent from the 6th to the 11th centuries. He is said to have lived in the 9th century and ruled from Mahishmati, in present-day Andhra Pradesh, India.

Another reference suggests that Lavitraj was a commander in the army of the Chalukya king, Vikramaditya II, who ruled in the late 11th century in the Deccan region of India. According to this account, Lavitraj led an army to defend against an invasion by the Hoysalas.
